description: We are Hack to Mars, a team focused on building secure, intelligent solutions for space exploration. We bring strong skills in AI, cybersecurity, embedded systems, and UI/UX design. We are looking for creative thinkers, data analysts, or 3D modelers to round out our crew. Join us if you want to tackle complex challenges, write great code, and aim for the Red Planet!
summary:
"Hack to Mars and Moon" is an innovative web platform designed to make lunar and Martian environments feel familiar by utilizing Egypt's unique desert landscapes as planetary analogs. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the project addresses the psychological hazards of spaceflight, such as isolation and unfamiliar terrain, by providing affordable Earth-based training grounds.  
​The platform features seven core tools, including an interactive Moon and Mars Explorer, a Moon/Mars Detector that scores Egyptian sites against planetary regions across six geological traits, 360-degree familiarization walks, and an Earth Sanctuary for stress-reduction breathing exercises. It also tracks user progress and provides scientific resources.  
​Financially, the project relies on a sustainable business model combining a free tier for public use, affordable pro subscriptions, institutional licenses, and guided desert workshops, targeting financial break-even by its third year. Its future roadmap outlines a phased approach ranging from geological validation and integration of real NASA satellite data to international scaling and virtual reality integration. Ultimately, the initiative bridges the gap between Earth and space exploration.
details:
Exploring the Moon and Mars presents challenges due to their unfamiliar geological and environmental conditions. To support planetary science education and pre-mission familiarization, Hack to Mars is an interactive web-based platform that connects Egypt’s geological landscapes with selected regions on Mars and the Moon.

The project examines seven Egyptian sites: the White Desert, Siwa Oasis and Qattara Depression, Jebel Uweinat, Faiyum, the Black Desert, Kamil Crater, and the Great Sand Sea. These are compared with eight extraterrestrial regions: Gale Crater, Jezero Crater, Tharsis Uplands, and Melas Chasma on Mars; and Mare Tranquillitatis, Linné Crater, Copernicus Crater, and the Lunar South Pole on the Moon. The comparison uses six geological parameters: aeolian erosion, aqueous alteration, iron-oxide staining, basaltic volcanism, impact features, and hyper-aridity. A similarity algorithm calculates the mean absolute difference between environmental profiles to identify the closest Martian and lunar analogs for each Egyptian site.

The platform combines an interactive geographical explorer, comparative visualizations, radar charts, and immersive panoramic environments. It also includes an Earth Sanctuary with guided breathing exercises, self-assessment tools for recording users’ perceived familiarity and comfort, and a dashboard that tracks their responses over time using locally stored data.

Hack to Mars integrates planetary science, data analysis, and interactive web technologies to make extraterrestrial environments more understandable and familiar. The similarity scores are illustrative values inspired by geological research, not experimentally measured data. The project provides a foundation for future development using validated datasets and user-based evaluation.

Keywords: Planetary Exploration, Terrestrial Analogs, Egyptian Geological Sites, Mars, Moon, Geological Similarity, Astronaut Familiarization, Interactive Platform.
